html:
The first Persian empire, founded by Cyrus the Great, stretching from Egypt and the Aegean to the Indus. It ran on satraps (governors), a royal road and a common coinage.

Its two invasions of Greece failed: at Marathon in 490 BCE, and at Salamis in 480 BCE under Xerxes. Later it shaped Greek affairs with money instead, paying for Sparta's fleet in the last years of the Peloponnesian War. Alexander the Great conquered it in 330 BCE.
